title: How New Zealand Banned Assault Rifles in Six Days

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我在《纽约时报》的每日简报 Dealbook 负责商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场，采访多位在商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani and many others live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、不做过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费阅读权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the Prime Minister of New Zealand promised to change the country's gun laws after a mass shooting last Friday.
sentences.zh: 今天，新西兰总理在经历上周五的大规模枪击事件后，承诺修改该国的枪支法律。

sentences.en: Less than a week later, she actually did it.
sentences.zh: 不到一周后，她真的做到了。

sentences.en: It's Friday, March 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月22日，星期五。

sentences.en: Jamie, in the immediate aftermath of the mosque attacks in New Zealand, what was the response from the country's prime minister?
sentences.zh: 杰米，在新西兰清真寺袭击事件发生后不久，该国总理作出了什么反应？

sentences.en: Jacinda Ardern came out and had a very sort of hastily arranged press briefing.
sentences.zh: 杰辛达·阿德恩出来举行了一场非常仓促安排的新闻发布会。

sentences.en: Sorry, let's go straight to the Prime Minister, Jacinda Ardern, speaking now.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，让我们直接连线正在发言的总理杰辛达·阿德恩。

sentences.en: And her first words were a complete and utter denouncement of what had happened.
sentences.zh: 她的第一句话就是对所发生事情彻底且坚决的谴责。

sentences.en: There is no place in New Zealand for such acts of extreme and unprecedented violence, which is, it is clear, this act was.
sentences.zh: 新西兰容不下这种极端的、史无前例的暴力行为，而这次事件显然就是这种行为。

sentences.en: She was very striking.
sentences.zh: 她当时的表态非常震撼。

sentences.en: Many of those who will have been directly affected by this shooting may be migrants to New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 许多在这场枪击中直接受影响的人可能是新西兰的移民。

sentences.en: They may even be refugees here.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可能是这里的难民。

sentences.en: They have chosen to make New Zealand their home, and it is their home.
sentences.zh: 他们选择将新西兰当作自己的家，这里就是他们的家。

sentences.en: She said they are us.
sentences.zh: 她说，他们就是我们。

sentences.en: The person who has perpetuated this violence against us is not.
sentences.zh: 对我们施加这种暴力的人则不是。

sentences.en: We reject everything about this sort of person.
sentences.zh: 我们坚决拒绝这种人的所作所为。

sentences.en: He is not one of us, the people who are part of our community, who have moved to this country, who have made lives here.
sentences.zh: 他不是我们的一员，不是那些融入我们社区、搬到这个国家并在这里生活的人。

sentences.en: These are the people who are a part of New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 这些人才是新西兰的一部分。

sentences.en: Jamie Terabay just returned from reporting in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 杰米·特拉拜刚刚从新西兰的报道一线归来。

sentences.en: So it was a really strong statement right from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以从一开始，这就是一个非常强有力的表态。

sentences.en: And what does she do next?
sentences.zh: 接下来她做了什么？

sentences.en: One of the first things she does is she gets on a plane and goes to Christchurch.
sentences.zh: 她做的第一件事就是登上飞机前往克赖斯特彻奇。

sentences.en: And at this point, all the domestic flights are grounded, because in New Zealand, you don't need to go through security checks to fly domestically.
sentences.zh: 当时所有的国内航班都停飞了，因为在新西兰，乘坐国内航班是不需要通过安全检查的。

sentences.en: You actually just walk straight onto the plane.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以直接走上飞机。

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这一点。

sentences.en: So she took a government plane and flew in.
sentences.zh: 所以她乘坐政府飞机飞了过去。

sentences.en: She arrived on the scene in Christchurch.
sentences.zh: 她抵达了克赖斯特彻奇的现场。

sentences.en: She went to a college campus that had been used as the sort of meeting point for the families and friends.
sentences.zh: 她去了一个被用作家属和朋友集合点的大学校园。

sentences.en: And, you know, I saw her walk in, and she had a blackhead scarf on.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我看到她走进来时，头上戴着一条黑色的头巾。

sentences.en: What did that signal to you?
sentences.zh: 那向你传递了什么信号？

sentences.en: It told me that she's culturally attuned, and she recognized that these were people in prayer, and this terrible thing happened to them and their families.
sentences.zh: 这告诉我她很有文化共情力，她认识到这些人正在祈祷，而他们和他们的家人遭遇了这件可怕的事。

sentences.en: You know, you've got to understand at this point, a lot of the people in that space still hadn't heard what had happened to their loved ones.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你必须明白，当时那个空间里的许多人仍然不知道他们的亲人遭遇了什么。

sentences.en: I met a 17-year-old boy there who kept on calling his dad's phone, and they kept on going to voicemail.
sentences.zh: 我在那里遇到一个17岁的男孩，他一直在给他爸爸的电话打电话，但总是转入语音信箱。

sentences.en: And this is the day after?
sentences.zh: 这是在事发后的第二天吗？

sentences.en: This is the day after, and he said to me that if he hadn't been told that his father was at hospital, then he could assume that he was dead.
sentences.zh: 这是事发第二天，他告诉我，如果没人告诉他父亲在医院，他就会以为父亲已经遇难了。

sentences.en: And so you have people in this state of anxiety and stress and grief, and she walked into this situation, and she just sort of said to the leaders who had gathered there,
sentences.zh: 所以当人们处于这种焦虑、压力和悲痛的状态时，她走进了这个环境，她对聚集在那里的领导人们说，

sentences.en: my time is yours, what do you want me to do, and they said to her, we want you to meet the families, and she did.
sentences.zh: 我的时间属于你们，你们想让我做什么，他们对她说，我们想让你去见见家属，她照做了。

sentences.en: She hugged people.
sentences.zh: 她拥抱了人们。

sentences.en: She hugged men and women, men who were dressed quite conservatively.
sentences.zh: 她拥抱了男人和女人，包括那些穿着相当保守的男性。

sentences.en: As-salamu alaykum.
sentences.zh: 阿萨兰姆阿莱库姆。

sentences.en: She began her words with, as-salamu alaykum, which is, you know, Arabic for peace be upon you, which is the standard Muslim greeting as well.
sentences.zh: 她以“阿萨兰姆阿莱库姆”开始发言，你知道，这是阿拉伯语“愿你平安”的意思，这也是穆斯林的标准问候语。

sentences.en: I'm here today to bring with me the grief of all of New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 我今天来这里，是带着整个新西兰的悲痛。

sentences.en: And there is huge grief in this nation.
sentences.zh: 这个国家有着巨大的悲痛。

sentences.en: And I'm here also to stand alongside you.
sentences.zh: 我来这里也是为了与你们站在一起。

sentences.en: And she was just there.
sentences.zh: 她就在那里。

sentences.en: She was very present, and she was connecting with all of these people emotionally.
sentences.zh: 她全身心投入，并在情感上与所有人紧密相连。

sentences.en: It was very moving to watch, and you could see that it had impacted her as well.
sentences.zh: 看着这一幕非常感人，你能看出这也对她产生了冲击。

sentences.en: And so we feel deeply in our hearts what has happened to you.
sentences.zh: 因此，你们所经历的一切，我们内心深处感同身受。

sentences.en: We feel grief.
sentences.zh: 我们感到悲痛。

sentences.en: We feel injustice.
sentences.zh: 我们感到不公。

sentences.en: We feel anger.
sentences.zh: 我们感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And we share that with you.
sentences.zh: 我们与你们感同身受。

sentences.en: Was any of this surprising to you, the way that she's approaching this horrible event in the first hours or so after?
sentences.zh: 对于她在事发最初几个小时内处理这一可怕事件的方式，你感到意外吗？

sentences.en: I think for anyone who has watched her, this is not a surprise at all.
sentences.zh: 我想对于任何关注她的人来说，这一点也不意外。

sentences.en: She came into politics this way.
sentences.zh: 她就是这样步入政坛的。

sentences.en: She is progressive.
sentences.zh: 她是进步派。

sentences.en: She's young.
sentences.zh: 她很年轻。

sentences.en: She refused to answer questions about whether she would have a child in office because she said you wouldn't be asking men those questions.
sentences.zh: 她拒绝回答关于她是否会在任期内生育的问题，因为她说你不会去问男性这个问题。

sentences.en: And then, of course, she later on, she did have a child in office, announced a tax package live from her couch while holding her 10-day-old baby.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，她后来确实在任内生了一个孩子，还抱着她10天大的宝宝在沙发上直播宣布了一项税收一揽子计划。

sentences.en: So I just wanted to share a few thoughts on that from the comfort of the couch sitting with little Niamh here with me.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想从舒适的沙发上，和这里的小妮芙一起，分享一些我的想法。

sentences.en: Took her three-month-old at the time to the UN.
sentences.zh: 她当时把三个月大的孩子带到了联合国。

sentences.en: And then, you know, just really sort of international darling because she's always sort of appeared to be a human being first and a politician second.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，她真正成为了国际宠儿，因为她总是表现得首先是一个人，其次才是一个政治家。

sentences.en: So given her, you know, really remarkable display of grief and sympathy over the weekend, that part of her personality was not unexpected.
sentences.zh: 因此，鉴于她在周末展现出的极其令人瞩目的悲痛与同情，她性格中的这一面并不出人意料。

sentences.en: What happened afterwards was...
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情是……

sentences.en: I want to speak specifically about the firearms used in this terrorist act.
sentences.zh: 我想专门谈谈这次恐怖袭击中使用的枪支。

sentences.en: That by the end of the weekend...
sentences.zh: 到周末结束时……

sentences.en: I can tell you one thing right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在就可以告诉你们一件事。

sentences.en: Our gun laws will change.
sentences.zh: 我们的枪支法律将会改变。

sentences.en: She had said that gun laws in New Zealand were going to change.
sentences.zh: 她曾说过新西兰的枪支法律将会改变。

sentences.en: And she said, they are going to change, not I am going to propose that they change.
sentences.zh: 她说的是“将会改变”，而不是“我将提议改变”。

sentences.en: It was unequivocal.
sentences.zh: 这是毋庸置疑的。

sentences.en: There was no dispute about what she said.
sentences.zh: 对于她所说的话没有任何争议。

sentences.en: And that was what was most surprising.
sentences.zh: 而这正是最令人惊讶的地方。

sentences.en: There have been attempts to change our laws in 2005, 2012, and after an inquiry in 2017.
sentences.zh: 过去曾在2005年、2012年以及2017年的一项调查后尝试修改我们的法律。

sentences.en: Now is the time for change.
sentences.zh: 现在是做出改变的时候了。

sentences.en: What did you think of that?
sentences.zh: 你对那个怎么看？

sentences.en: I remember hearing her say that and thinking, sure you will.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时听到她这么说时心想，你当然会这么说。

sentences.en: And being quite skeptical.
sentences.zh: 并且对此相当怀疑。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not something that you imagine that would happen so quickly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不是那种你会想象能发生得这么快的事情。

sentences.en: And she doesn't have a major, like, majority in her government.
sentences.zh: 而且她在政府里并没有占据绝对多数。

sentences.en: So she was finishing the weekend.
sentences.zh: 所以她当时正要结束这个周末。

sentences.en: This weekend of grief.
sentences.zh: 这个充满悲伤的周末。

sentences.en: You know, candlelight vigils and people from around the country came to Christchurch to show their sympathy and their support for the Muslim community.
sentences.zh: 你知道，烛光守夜活动以及来自全国各地的人们来到克赖斯特彻奇，表达他们对穆斯林社区的同情与支持。

sentences.en: Then to have her say, the gun laws are going to change, before she's even met with her cabinet.
sentences.zh: 然后她甚至在与内阁会面之前就说，枪支法律将要改变。

sentences.en: It was really, really striking.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常、非常震撼。

sentences.en: So how does she go about trying to actually do this?
sentences.zh: 那么她是如何着手去真正实现这一点的呢？

sentences.en: Look, I think that she had a lot of momentum.
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为她当时拥有很大的势头。

sentences.en: I think that she wanted to act quickly.
sentences.zh: 我认为她希望迅速采取行动。

sentences.en: And for her, in New Zealand, they had a template very close by.
sentences.zh: 对她而言，在新西兰，他们有一个非常近的模板。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: On the island of Tasmania, the worst massacre in Australian history is finally over.
sentences.zh: 在塔斯马尼亚岛，澳大利亚历史上最严重的大屠杀终于结束了。

sentences.en: At least 34 people were killed and four others critically wounded when a 29-year-old gunman with a history of mental problems opened fire in a popular tourist area.
sentences.zh: 一名有精神病史的29岁枪手在一个受欢迎的旅游区开枪，造成至少34人死亡、4人重伤。

sentences.en: The carnage came to an end only this morning after the gunman caught fire following a 12-hour standoff with police.
sentences.zh: 在与警方对峙12小时后，枪手纵火焚烧自己，这场惨剧直到今天早晨才告一段落。

sentences.en: He's alive and in custody today, Monday, April the 29th, 1996.
sentences.zh: 他今天（4月29日星期一）还活着并已被拘留。

sentences.en: We had a conservative government in charge at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我们执政的是一个保守派政府。

sentences.en: The Prime Minister, John Howard, tonight detailed sweeping plans to reform Australia's national gun laws,
sentences.zh: 总理约翰·霍华德今晚详细阐述了改革澳大利亚国家枪支法律的全面计划，

sentences.en: which could mean the introduction of a one-off tax to buy back illegal weapons.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着引入一次性税收以回购非法武器。

sentences.en: In the wake of Port Arthur, Mr Howard has also promised to consider new restrictions on violent videos and computer games.
sentences.zh: 在亚瑟港惨案发生后，霍华德先生还承诺考虑对暴力录像和电脑游戏实施新的限制。

sentences.en: Which normally wouldn't be so quick to move on things like this.
sentences.zh: 这通常不会在类似事情上行动得这么快。

sentences.en: I thought to myself, if I don't use the authority of this newly acquired office to do something, the Australian people are entitled to think, well, this bloke's not up to much.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，如果我不利用这个新获得的办公室的权力做点什么，澳大利亚人民完全有权认为，这家伙没什么大作为。

sentences.en: And so when you have that political will, when you have that support from the people in charge, despite the fact that there was a very vocal gun lobby in Australia,
sentences.zh: 因此，当你拥有这种政治意愿，当你拥有掌权者的支持，尽管澳大利亚存在一个非常直言不讳的枪支游说集团，

sentences.en: they managed to push through the bans on all of these weapons and implement a buyback and a gun amnesty.
sentences.zh: 他们还是设法强行通过了对所有这些武器的禁令，并实施了回购和枪支特赦计划。

sentences.en: People used to say to me, you've violated my human rights by taking away my gun.
sentences.zh: 过去常有人对我说，你拿走我的枪就是侵犯了我的基本人权。

sentences.en: And I'd say, look, I understand that, but will you please understand the argument?
sentences.zh: 我会说，听着，我理解这一点，但请你理解这个论点好吗？

sentences.en: The greatest human right of all is to live a safe life without fear of random murder.
sentences.zh: 所有基本人权中最伟大的一项，是过上一种安全的生活，而不必担惊受怕遭遇随机谋杀。

sentences.en: And it worked.
sentences.zh: 而且它成功了。

sentences.en: It is incontestable that gun-related homicides have fallen quite significantly in Australia.
sentences.zh: 无可争辩的是，澳大利亚与枪支相关的凶杀案已经显著下降。

sentences.en: Incontestable.
sentences.zh: 无可争辩。

sentences.en: I mean, if you had 13 mass shootings before Port Arthur and you had none since, isn't that evidence?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果在亚瑟港之前发生了13起大规模枪击事件而此后一次也没有，这难道不是证据吗？

sentences.en: Or are we expected to believe that that was all magically going to happen?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们该相信这一切都是靠魔法自然发生的？

sentences.en: There hasn't been any kind of mass shooting like that in Australia since.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，澳大利亚再也没有发生过那种类型的大规模枪击事件。

sentences.en: So it was something that was feasible and successful.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件可行且成功的事情。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权。

sentences.en: On 15 March, the nation witnessed a terrorist attack that demonstrated the weakness of New Zealand's gun laws.
sentences.zh: 3月15日，这个国家目睹了一场恐怖袭击，它暴露了新西兰枪支法律的脆弱性。

sentences.en: So how does this week end for the prime minister?
sentences.zh: 那么，这位总理本周将如何收尾？

sentences.en: So she'd spent the week mourning publicly, but also behind doors, talking, consulting with her cabinet.
sentences.zh: 她花了一周时间进行公开哀悼，但也闭门与内阁进行讨论和协商。

sentences.en: But she's also reaching out to the opposition.
sentences.zh: 但她也在向反对党伸出援手。

sentences.en: She wants to make sure that this is a unified effort.
sentences.zh: 她希望确保这是一次联合行动。

sentences.en: She wants to make sure that everyone's feeling included.
sentences.zh: 她希望确保每个人都感到被包容。

sentences.en: And beyond that, it's also a question about national unity as well.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，这也是一个关于国家团结的问题。

sentences.en: The time for the mass and easy availability of these weapons must end.
sentences.zh: 大众轻易获取这些武器的时代必须结束了。

sentences.en: And, you know, by Thursday, she came out and she declared...
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，到了星期四，她出来并宣布……

sentences.en: And today, they will.
sentences.zh: 而今天，他们会的。

sentences.en: ...that her government has banned all the different kinds of weapons that were used in that attack.
sentences.zh: ……她的政府已经禁止了在那次袭击中使用的所有不同类型的武器。

sentences.en: Today, I'm announcing that New Zealand will ban all military-style semi-automatic weapons.
sentences.zh: 今天，我宣布新西兰将禁止所有军用半自动武器。

sentences.en: We will also ban all assault rifles.
sentences.zh: 我们还将禁止所有突击步枪。

sentences.en: We will ban all high-capacity magazines.
sentences.zh: 我们将禁止所有大容量弹匣。

sentences.en: We will ban all parts with the ability to convert semi-automatic or any other type of firearm into a military-style semi-automatic weapon.
sentences.zh: 我们将禁止所有能够将半自动武器或任何其他类型枪支转换为军用半自动武器的零部件。

sentences.en: In short, every semi-automatic weapon used in the terrorist attack on Friday will be banned in this country.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，周五恐怖袭击中所使用的每一款半自动武器都将在本国被禁。

sentences.en: And, you know, there was going to be a buyback for everyone who has those weapons already.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对于所有已经拥有这些武器的人，将会有一个回购计划。

sentences.en: So, you know, people who spent over $1,000 on an AR-15 that they use at the range, they have to turn it in and they'll be given money.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，那些花了一千多美元买了一支在靶场使用的 AR-15 的人，必须把它上交并会获得金钱补偿。

sentences.en: It's going to cost the New Zealand government about $140 million to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 新西兰政府将花费大约1.4亿美元来支付这笔费用。

sentences.en: But they've literally decided all of these things within the space of two or three days.
sentences.zh: 但他们在短短两三天内就做出了所有这些决定。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: In six days, actually a little bit less than six days after a mass shooting, the prime minister of New Zealand has fundamentally changed the country's gun laws,
sentences.zh: 在大规模枪击事件发生的六天内——实际上还不到六天，新西兰总理就从根本上改变了该国的枪支法律，

sentences.en: banned certain weapons, restricted access to others.
sentences.zh: 禁用了某些武器，并限制了对其他武器的获取。

sentences.en: I mean, that's kind of staggering.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直太震撼了。

sentences.en: It's huge.
sentences.zh: 这太巨大了。

sentences.en: Jamie, what explains how this unfolded, how quickly it unfolded in New Zealand in the aftermath of a mass shooting compared with how it usually happens in a place like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 杰米，这究竟是怎么回事？与美国在发生大规模枪击事件后的通常情况相比，为什么新西兰在枪击事件后能如此迅速地做出反应？

sentences.en: after a mass shooting here?
sentences.zh: 也就是这里发生枪击案之后？

sentences.en: Well, I think one of the first things that you have to look at is the gun culture within both of those countries.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为首先需要审视的因素之一就是这两个国家的枪支文化。

sentences.en: In New Zealand, you are very heavily regulated.
sentences.zh: 在新西兰，枪支受到极度严格的管制。

sentences.en: If you want to apply for a license, you have to have background checks.
sentences.zh: 如果你想申请持枪证，你必须通过背景调查。

sentences.en: You have to show that you are mentally fit to have one.
sentences.zh: 你必须证明自己在精神上适合拥有枪支。

sentences.en: You have to have two references and those references get interviewed.
sentences.zh: 你必须提供两个证明人，而且这些证明人会接受面谈。

sentences.en: Your partner or your family member gets interviewed.
sentences.zh: 你的伴侣或家庭成员也会接受面谈。

sentences.en: Two references as in people have to write or be...
sentences.zh: 两个证明人是指人们必须写信或者……

sentences.en: People have to stand up for you and then they get interviewed.
sentences.zh: 人们必须为你担保，然后他们会接受面谈。

sentences.en: So they need to show why they support you getting a license.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要说明为什么支持你获得持枪证。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: And then for the particular gun that you want, you then also have to get a license for that particular weapon.
sentences.zh: 对于你想要的特定枪支，你还得专门为这种特定武器申请许可证。

sentences.en: And then if you get a traffic violation, if the police get called to your house, that all goes into the database.
sentences.zh: 如果你有交通违章记录，或者警察接到报警去你家，这些都会录入数据库。

sentences.en: And if the police feel that you're coming to their attention a bit too much, they'll come in and they'll check in on you.
sentences.zh: 如果警察觉得你引起他们注意的频率过高，他们就会上门来对你进行回访。

sentences.en: So this is a heavily regulated gun culture.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种管制极其严格的枪支文化。

sentences.en: This is a country where you have to prove that you are able to have a weapon and that you deserve to have one.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家，你必须证明自己有能力拥有武器，并且你配得上拥有它。

sentences.en: You are responsible enough to have one.
sentences.zh: 你足够负责任去拥有它。

sentences.en: And of course, in the U.S., we have the Second Amendment, which has created a legal sense that gun ownership is a natural born right.
sentences.zh: 当然，在美国，我们有宪法第二修正案，它在法律上确立了一种观念，即拥有枪支是天生的人权。

sentences.en: It's something that you just possess as an American.
sentences.zh: 这是你作为美国人理所当然拥有的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And in some states in America, you can carry a weapon on you.
sentences.zh: 在美国的某些州，你可以随身携带武器。

sentences.en: That would be unheard of in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 这在新西兰是闻所未闻的。

sentences.en: You are only allowed to take your weapon when you're firing it on the range or if you're, you know, sort of doing a cull of animals on your farm or something or you're hunting.
sentences.zh: 你只有在靶场射击时，或者在农场清理动物、打猎时，才能携带武器。

sentences.en: So there is very specific places you can use your weapon.
sentences.zh: 因此，你只能在非常特定的场所有效使用你的武器。

sentences.en: And there is a significant number of gun owners in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 新西兰的枪支拥有者数量也相当可观。

sentences.en: There's about 250,000 in a population of 5 million.
sentences.zh: 在500万人口中大约有25万持枪者。

sentences.en: But by and large, it's not an assault rifle culture.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，这不是一种突击步枪文化。

sentences.en: It's more of a sportsmanship shooting precision target competition.
sentences.zh: 它更偏向于运动射击和精密靶标比赛。

sentences.en: Actually, New Zealand hosted the World Shooting Championship earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 事实上，新西兰在今年早些时候主办了世界射击锦标赛。

sentences.en: So the notion of kind of self-defense, owning a gun, to use it against a criminal, it's not the culture.
sentences.zh: 因此，诸如自我防卫、拥有一把枪来对付罪犯之类的概念，并不是这里的文化。

sentences.en: No, the rate of homicides in New Zealand, especially by guns, is very low.
sentences.zh: 是的，新西兰的凶杀率，尤其是涉枪凶杀率，非常低。

sentences.en: And it's, yeah, it is definitely more of we have guns for sport rather than guns for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，我们拥有枪支绝对是为了运动，而不是为了自卫。

sentences.en: Does New Zealand have an NRA type of lobby and political power?
sentences.zh: 新西兰有没有类似美国全国步枪协会（NRA）的游说集团和政治势力？

sentences.en: It has people who are pro-guns, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，那里也有支持枪支的人。

sentences.en: There are people who run blogs that are somewhat influential.
sentences.zh: 有些人运营着一些有一定影响力的博客。

sentences.en: But the degree to which the NRA in the United States operates and lobbies, there's just nothing like that in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 但就美国NRA那种运作和游说的程度而言，新西兰根本没有与之相似的东西。

sentences.en: The head of the NRA in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 新西兰NRA的负责人。

sentences.en: There is an NRA.
sentences.zh: 确实有一个NRA。

sentences.en: There is an NRA in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 新西兰确实有一个NRA。

sentences.en: It's completely different.
sentences.zh: 它完全不同。

sentences.en: Actually, last year, they were considering changing their name because they didn't want the association.
sentences.zh: 事实上，去年他们曾考虑改名，因为他们不想沾染这种关联。

sentences.en: What did they find that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得美国的

sentences.en: NRA is too much of for them?
sentences.zh: NRA对他们来说有什么过分的地方吗？

sentences.en: There's a couple of different things.
sentences.zh: 有几个不同的方面。

sentences.en: They thought the NRA in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们认为美国的NRA

sentences.en: was extremely political.
sentences.zh: 极具政治色彩。

sentences.en: But they also said that the NRA in America embraces all the different rifles, et cetera, whereas they were just concerned with thousand-yard shooting, precision target rifles.
sentences.zh: 但他们也表示，美国的NRA包容了所有不同类型的步枪等等，而他们只关心千码射击和精密靶标步枪。

sentences.en: They didn't do military rifles.
sentences.zh: 他们不涉及军用步枪。

sentences.en: They didn't do assault rifles.
sentences.zh: 他们不涉及突击步枪。

sentences.en: And they just thought that was a very clear difference between them and the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们只是觉得，他们与美国之间存在着非常明显的区别。

sentences.en: A really important point that the head of the NRA in New Zealand told me is that gun ownership in New Zealand is a privilege.
sentences.zh: 新西兰NRA负责人告诉我一个非常重要的观点，即在新西兰，拥有枪支是一种特权。

sentences.en: It is not a right.
sentences.zh: 它不是一种权利。

sentences.en: It's something that the government allows you to have if you pass through these rigorous checks.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过了这些严格的审查，政府才允许你拥有它。

sentences.en: So it's not actually within the gun culture in New Zealand to sort of rail against the idea that those guns would be taken away.
sentences.zh: 因此，新西兰的枪支文化中，实际上并不存在那种抗议收缴枪支的想法。

sentences.en: What you're describing is a state of national horror after a massacre in New Zealand that galvanized the entire country to change their gun laws.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的是新西兰在发生大屠杀后陷入的全国悲痛状态，这种悲痛促使整个国家团结起来修改枪支法律。

sentences.en: And to an American, that still feels kind of unfathomable and impractical because we have had so many of these mass shootings and massacres.
sentences.zh: 对美国人来说，这仍然让人觉得有点不可思议且不切实际，因为我们经历过如此多的惨烈枪击和屠杀事件。

sentences.en: So I think that one of the things that strikes Australians and New Zealanders whenever there is a mass shooting in America is how can this still be going on?
sentences.zh: 所以我想，每当美国发生大规模枪击事件时，澳大利亚人和新西兰人脑海中浮现的一个问题就是：这种情况怎么还能继续发生？

sentences.en: And in the sense that Australia was quick to achieve consensus, New Zealand was quick to achieve consensus.
sentences.zh: 就像澳大利亚迅速达成共识一样，新西兰也迅速达成了共识。

sentences.en: And in the United States, consensus is so far out of reach.
sentences.zh: 而在美国，达成共识简直遥不可及。

sentences.en: You cannot have unity around gun culture and gun control if you don't have unity within the community.
sentences.zh: 如果社区内部无法达成一致，你就无法围绕枪支文化和枪支管制形成团结。

sentences.en: New Zealand is a very inclusive society.
sentences.zh: 新西兰是一个极具包容性的社会。

sentences.en: It's used to people coming from different countries and assimilating and making lives there.
sentences.zh: 它习惯了来自不同国家的人们融入其中并在那里生活。

sentences.en: These are people who are New Zealanders firSt.
sentences.zh: 这些人首先都是新西兰人。

sentences.en: And so when Jacinda Ardern said, these people are us, they are us, she included everyone all together in this.
sentences.zh: 所以当杰辛达·阿德恩说“这些人就是我们，他们就是我们”时，她把每一个人都紧紧凝聚在这个集体中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The immigrants, MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 移民，穆斯林。

sentences.en: It shocked everyone.
sentences.zh: 这震惊了所有人。

sentences.en: So she had the political will.
sentences.zh: 所以她拥有政治意愿。

sentences.en: She had, you know, the politicians, the opposition on board.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她得到了政客们和反对派的支持。

sentences.en: She had the people supporting her, even gun owners.
sentences.zh: 她得到了人民的支持，甚至包括枪支所有者。

sentences.en: Gun owners supported the decision to take away their guns.
sentences.zh: 枪支拥有者支持收缴他们枪支的决定。

sentences.en: Even gun retailers and hunting groups and fishing groups agreed.
sentences.zh: 甚至枪支零售商、狩猎团体和钓鱼团体也表示赞同。

sentences.en: That this was something that needed to be done.
sentences.zh: 认为这是必须要做的事情。

sentences.en: Finally, I want to repeat a message I have consistently shared since announcing our laws would change.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想重申自我宣布修改法律以来一直传达的信息。

sentences.en: We do have guns in New Zealand that are used for legitimate purposes by responsible owners.
sentences.zh: 我们在新西兰确实有用于合法目的、由负责任的枪主持有的枪支。

sentences.en: I've been steadfast in my belief that the vast majority of these owners will support what we are doing here today.
sentences.zh: 我始终坚信，绝大多数枪主都会支持我们今天在这里所做的事情。

sentences.en: Because it's about all of us.
sentences.zh: 因为这关乎我们每一个人。

sentences.en: It's in the national interest and it's about safety.
sentences.zh: 这符合国家利益，也关乎安全。

sentences.en: I will work hard to retain that support as we work on the remaining tranches of reform that we must make to prevent an act of terror happening in our country ever again.
sentences.zh: 我将努力保持这种支持，同时推进我们必须完成的其余改革步骤，以防止我们国家再次发生恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: Jamie, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 杰米，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: The message that President Trump has given the world is that America stands by Israel.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统向世界传递的信息是，美国坚定支持以色列。

sentences.en: On Thursday, President Trump said that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周四，特朗普总统表示，美国

sentences.en: should recognize Israel's authority over the Golan Heights, one of the world's most disputed territories, in a reversal of decades of American policy
sentences.zh: 应当承认以色列对戈兰高地的管辖权——这是世界上争议最大的领土之一，此举推翻了几十年来的美国政策

sentences.en: and in violation of a United Nations resolution.
sentences.zh: 并违反了联合国决议。

sentences.en: Israel seized the Golan Heights from Syria in 1967 and effectively annexed it in 1981.
sentences.zh: 以色列于1967年从叙利亚手中夺取了戈兰高地，并于1981年实际将其吞并。

sentences.en: But neither the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但无论是美国

sentences.en: nor the U.N.
sentences.zh: 还是联合国

sentences.en: consider it a part of Israel, arguing its fate should be determined in a larger negotiation over peace with Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 都不认为它是以色列的一部分，并主张其命运应在关于巴勒斯坦和平的更大规模谈判中决定。

sentences.en: This is the eve of Purim and we have a miracle of Purim.
sentences.zh: 今天是普珥节前夜，我们迎来了普珥节的奇迹。

sentences.en: We call it Nest Purim.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“新普珥节”。

sentences.en: President Trump has just made history.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统刚刚创造了历史。

sentences.en: The decision was made at the request of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is locked in a close re-election battle, faces a series of indictments,
sentences.zh: 这一决定是在以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的要求下做出的，他目前正陷入激烈的连任选战中，面临一系列起诉，

sentences.en: and could benefit politically from the policy change.
sentences.zh: 并且能从这一政策转变中获得政治利益。

sentences.en: During a news conference in Israel with Secretary of State Mike Pompeo,
sentences.zh: 在与国务卿迈克·蓬佩奥于以色列举行的联合新闻发布会上，

sentences.en: Netanyahu thanked the Trump administration for the decision.
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡对特朗普政府做出这一决定表示感谢。

sentences.en: I called him.
sentences.zh: 我给他打了电话。

sentences.en: I thanked him on behalf of the people of Israel.
sentences.zh: 我代表以色列人民向他表示感谢。

sentences.en: He recognized Israel's sovereignty over the Golan Heights.
sentences.zh: 他承认了以色列对戈兰高地的主权。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that safety features that might have prevented the Boeing 737 MAX 8 from crashing in Indonesia and Ethiopia were optional ones for which Boeing charged extra
sentences.zh: 据《泰晤士报》报道，本可以阻止波音737 MAX 8客机在印度尼西亚和埃塞俄比亚坠毁的安全功能，其实是波音公司额外收费的选配项目

sentences.en: and which were not present on the doomed planes.
sentences.zh: 并且在失事的飞机上并未安装这些设备。

sentences.en: The optional features help catch erroneous readings from sensors that could prompt the plane's flight control system to force down the nose of the plane,
sentences.zh: 这些选配功能有助于捕捉传感器传来的错误读数，而这些错误读数可能会促使飞机的飞行控制系统强行压低机头，

sentences.en: a suspected cause of the crash in Indonesia, and a possible explanation for what happened in Ethiopia.
sentences.zh: 这被认为是印尼坠机事件的潜在原因，也是对埃塞俄比亚发生事故的一种可能解释。

sentences.en: The Daily is produced by Theo Balcom, Lindsay Garrison, Rachel Quester, Annie Brown, Andy Mills,
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》由西奥·巴尔科姆、林赛·加里森、雷切尔·奎斯特、安妮·布朗、安迪·米尔斯、

sentences.zh: 艾克·斯里兹-卡纳拉贾、克莱尔·特内斯凯特、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊、杰西卡·钟、亚历山德拉·李·杨

sentences.en: and Jonathan Wolfe, and edited by Paige Cowan, Larissa Anderson, and Wendy Doerr.
sentences.zh: 以及乔纳森·沃尔夫制作，并由佩奇·考恩、拉里萨·安德森和温迪·多尔编辑。

sentences.zh: 我们的技术经理是布拉德·费舍尔。

sentences.zh: 特别感谢萨姆·多尔米克、米凯拉·布沙尔和斯特拉·陈。

sentences.en: And today, we say farewell to Ike Sreez-Khanaraja, who will miss dearly.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们向艾克·斯里兹-卡纳拉贾道别，我们将深深怀念他。

sentences.en: Thank you, Ike.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，艾克。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 我们周一再见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的政治机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎进来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党便陷入了一场激烈、混乱且有时令人热血沸腾的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的播客《都会》中，我和萨拉·科尼格将带您了解那些试图维持影响力却最终失去控制的人们的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都会》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何平台上收听。
